12.2b — Placeholder Jam: Day 2 + Year Retro

The last B day of the year. If the placeholder jam got its topic, today ships it and shows it. Either way, the class ends with the year's retro — the one document that tells September-you what you learned, written by the person who actually learned it.

Ship (if jam) ~30 min

If a topic landed: the 10.1e polish + freeze contract, compressed: feedback pass on every action, three sounds, 30-second first impression, BUILD the build, test the build. Then a ten-minute mini-showcase (arcade row, star votes: 10.1f contract). Every jam this year ended the same way on purpose: shipping is the skill; the theme was the excuse.

If flex: finish yesterday's portfolio item (12.2a) and push it. The projects page with real entries IS the class's final artifact.

Year Retro ~25 min

Write it, then say it. Both count. The five questions:

  1. The pattern inventory: name every pattern you personally own now — cooldown, state machine, singleton, events, list traversal, bounds checks, input → behavior → output. Count them. That count is your year in one number.
  2. The moment the floor tilted: the single day the class stopped being "assignments" and became "my game" — for most people it is the 7.5a sketch or the first 8.2a phase change. Why yours?
  3. The constraint lesson: your three jams' constraints (2-button, lists, grid) — which one made you most creative, and what does that say about your NEXT project's constraints?
  4. The data lesson: when did numbers beat vibes? (9.5a's insight, or your 11.4b error table, or a playtest that humbled a favorite idea.)
  5. The September letter: three sentences to the person who forked the starter in 1.1a. What do they not know that you now know? What should they stop worrying about? What should they start on day one?

Tinker: The last commit

  1. YEAR_RETRO.md in your repo: the five answers, the pattern inventory with file references, the September letter at the bottom.
  2. Tag it: git tag year-one && git push --tags. That tag is your portfolio's proof-of-work — a year, versioned.
  3. Then close the laptop. The boss is dead, the exam is taken, the jams are shipped, and the year pushed. Congratulations — this was "sorta your first on your own experience," and it was yours.

Reflect: the September letter, in three sentences

What does September-you not know that you now know, what should they stop worrying about, and what should they start on day one?

Checkpoint — the year, complete:

  • Whatever the placeholder became, it is shipped and pushed
  • YEAR_RETRO.md written, with the pattern inventory and the September letter
  • Repo tagged year-one — the whole course, versioned
  • You can name, from memory, what you know how to make
